title: The Future Active and the Gerundive
subtitle: amātūrus / amandus. Intention versus obligation.
objectives: Translate future active as 'about to X'.
Translate gerundive as 'must be X-ed' or 'to be X-ed'.

sections.heading: Future active and gerundive
sections.body:
Future active: perfect stem + -ūrus, -a, -um:
  amātūrus — about to love

Gerundive: present stem + -ndus, -a, -um:
  amandus — must be loved, to be loved

Caesar writes: moritūrus tē salūtat. — He who is about to die salutes you.
Cato writes: Carthāgō dēlenda est. — Carthage must be destroyed.

items.prompt: Form the future participle of dūcō (dūxī).

words.gloss: The man is about to come.
